key_insight: SequenTx combines a virtual-cell model of tumour cell-state transitions with reinforcement learning to design adaptive, sequential drug regimens that steer tumour evolution away from resistant states. The approach produces treatment policies that proactively manage therapy-induced evolution rather than react to it.
problem_solved: Addresses the challenge of therapy-induced tumour evolution and drug resistance by providing a computational method to plan multi-step treatment sequences that account for dynamic cellular state changes over time.
method: Build a virtual-cell-inspired simulator that models dynamic cellular state transitions under different drugs and microenvironmental conditions.
Train a reinforcement learning agent to choose sequential treatment actions (drug choices/timings) using rewards that reflect tumour control, resistance minimization, and clinical constraints.
Evaluate learned policies in silico to compare outcomes (tumour burden, resistance emergence) vs. standard or static treatment schedules.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a concrete example of applying RL to a complex, temporally-evolving biological system, highlighting design of simulators, reward shaping, and policy evaluation for high-stakes sequential decision problems. The framework can inspire robust RL methods for other evolving systems and offline policy validation pipelines.

paper_title: Reinforcement learning-based design of sequential drug treatment targeting the evolving tumour landscape with SequenTx
